title: test(organizations): the two upload-wall suites run under 10 s (two #23184 rows)
body:
Refs #23184 (organizations rows: storage-upload-organization-change, storage-upload-door-ownership)
Clause-②: no

## Rows answered

Both rows of the card's `@objectstack/organizations` list:

- `src/storage-upload-organization-change.wall.test.ts`, listed at 15.9 s (run `38222448090`);
- `src/storage-upload-door-ownership.wall.test.ts`, listed at 15.2 s (run `38222448090`).

The pin is the next refresh PR's list: it should name neither file. The card stays open for its other rows: the three remaining `plugin-auth` rows (org-create-posture-gate, implicit-account-linking, dev-admin-seed-credential-gate) and the two `plugin-security` rows.

The diff is tests only, +116 / -0: one new test-only helper, `src/__tests__/upload-wall-warm-up.testkit.ts`, and 7 added lines in each of the two files (an import, a 4-line comment and one module-scope call). No production file, option, constant, timeout or export changes. Every `it(`, `describe(`, `expect(`, `beforeAll(` and `afterAll(` line in both files is byte-identical to the base and in the same order.

## Which number this PR reads

The graded number is the file's module line in CI's `test-core.log`: vitest's default reporter, hooks plus cases, collection excluded. Earlier slices of this card read the JSON reporter's `endTime - startTime` as the same number. For these two files it is not: that span covers the cases only, and most of these files' wall sits in `beforeAll`. At the base, the JSON span read 1.36 to 1.39 s and 0.47 to 0.59 s, while the module line read 5.1 to 6.4 s and 4.4 to 4.9 s. Every figure below is the module line.

## Where the time went

Both files boot the same walled stack in `beforeAll`: `bootStack` with this package's `OrganizationsPlugin` and the real `StorageServicePlugin`, under `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated` and `OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY=invite-only`. A probe at the base (a temporary file, deleted; one run per shape) repeated each file's arrangement three times in one process and timed every step:

| step | organization-change shape: boot 1 / 2 / 3 | door-ownership shape: boot 1 / 2 / 3 |
|:--|--:|--:|
| `bootStack` | **3249** / 941 / 1172 ms | **3788** / 948 / 896 ms |
| seeded admin `signIn` | 188 / 144 / 126 ms | 177 / 137 / 130 ms |
| the file's own arrangement (`get-session`, sign-ups, invitation, organizations, `set-active`) | 115 / 89 / 88 ms | 673 / 438 / 416 ms |

So the first boot in a process costs 2.3 to 2.8 s more than every later one, and the difference is first use, not the boot. The default datasource's driver and better-auth's entries are `import()`ed lazily from inside the boot, sql.js compiles its WASM, and every path runs cold. The file's `beforeAll` was the first boot in its process, so it paid all of that inside a clocked hook. The cases themselves were about 1.1 to 1.4 s (organization-change) and 0.47 to 0.59 s (door-ownership) of real HTTP round trips, and neither file waits on a timer.

## What changed

Each file now calls `await warmUpUploadWallBoot()` once at module scope, so the first load is paid during collection. This follows the AGENTS.md convention that clocked windows measure behaviour, never loading. The helper is this package's copy of `@objectstack/verify`'s `warmUpBoot` (`packages/verify/src/boot-warm-up.testkit.ts`, landed in `72329942f9` as the `@objectstack/verify` slice of a sibling test-budget card; that package does not export it):

- It boots a throwaway app (no objects) on the same composition, signs the seeded admin in, signs one member up, and stops.
- It uses plugin instances of its own, its own in-memory database and its own storage root.
- It sets the same two environment variables as the files. `bootStack` sets `NODE_ENV` itself before it loads anything, so a module that reads its environment once at first load reads the same values as at the base.
- Afterwards it restores the whole environment, the variables the boot set included, so the file's first hook starts from the environment it started from before this change.
- What stays warm is process-level only: the module registry, sql.js's compiled WASM and the JIT.

The files' own `beforeAll` still boots, signs in and arranges exactly as before, inside the clock.

## Measurements

Each figure is the vitest module line: `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 FILE --reporter=default --reporter=json`, in `packages/plugins/organizations`, under `os-verify-lock`, on a shared 4-vCPU box. In the final rounds, before and after were interleaved at the final head, with the before leg being the base file copied to a temporary name (deleted afterwards), so both legs saw the same load.

| file | before, base `43d75ef274` alone (load 0.8 to 1.6) | before, interleaved at `56e42d33bf` (load 1.1 to 1.9) | after, interleaved at `56e42d33bf` | median after |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|--:|
| storage-upload-organization-change | 6412 / 5229 / 5137 ms | 4143 / 4822 / 4166 ms | 2206 / 2756 / 2178 ms | **2.21 s** |
| storage-upload-door-ownership | 4924 / 4805 / 4366 ms | 4086 / 3838 / 3623 ms | 1975 / 1927 / 1823 ms | **1.93 s** |

**What remains in the clock**, from a probe of the first cut `e4409fcac0` (temporary copies, deleted):

- One warm boot, about 0.9 to 1.2 s, whose largest part is ObjectQL's start (440 to 578 ms).
- Real production-parameter scrypt: 2 derivations (207 ms) in organization-change and 4 (409 ms) in door-ownership, all in `beforeAll`.
- The cases' HTTP round trips: about 1.0 to 1.3 s and 0.45 to 0.57 s.

**The load is moved, not removed.** vitest's whole-file `Duration` (collection plus run) went from 27.1 to 29.3 s before to 27.6 to 31.6 s after in the final rounds. The `import` phase grew from 22.8 to 24.3 s to 25.5 to 28.7 s. The extra second is the throwaway boot's own work. What the change buys is that no hook or case clock contains a cold load any more. It does not make the package's test job faster.

**CI projection.** The per-file CI captures of recent hourly runs are NOT MEASURED: this container has no authenticated read of the timing artifacts, and the card's two previous slices measured that their blob-storage redirect is refused here. The ratios therefore come from the card's own readings:

| file | card reading | ratio, over the interleaved before median | projected | ratio, over the standalone base median | projected | at a 4.0 ratio |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| organization-change | 15.9 s | 3.82 | **8.4 s** | 3.04 | 6.7 s | 8.8 s |
| door-ownership | 15.2 s | 3.96 | **7.6 s** | 3.16 | 6.1 s | 7.7 s |

All projections are under the 10 s line. Organization-change has the smaller margin. Its remaining wall is one warm boot plus ten cases of real requests against one uploader, which no further test-side change shortens without changing what the file measures.

**Considered and not done:**

- A scrypt memo, as in the `plugin-auth` slices. Only the seeded admin's sign-in would hit it, because every sign-up draws a fresh salt. That saves about 0.1 s per file, which is not worth patching a builtin.
- `describe.concurrent`. The organization-change cases share one uploader whose active organization is session state, so they cannot overlap. The door-ownership cases total about 0.5 s.
- Moving each file's own boot to module scope. That would take behaviour out of the clock, not loading.
- A declared budget. It does not apply, because both projections are under the line.

## Proof that every case still runs and still asserts the same

- **Case lists:** 10 of 10 and 10 of 10 passed in every run, before and after.
- **Static lines:** the `it(` / `describe(` / `expect(` / `beforeAll(`-`afterAll(` lines are byte-identical to the base and in order. Organization-change has 10 / 5 / 59 / 2 and door-ownership has 10 / 4 / 44 / 2. The diff to each file is 7 added lines and nothing removed.
- **Runtime assertions:** temporary instrumented copies of the base and head files (deleted) recorded `expect.getState().assertionCalls` per case. The per-case counts are identical: 127 assertions over 10 cases for organization-change, and 86 over 10 for door-ownership. No case asserts nothing.
- **The same arrangement, and nothing shared (the same copies):**
  - At the end of each file's `beforeAll`, base and head read the same values. That covers the row count and column set of `sys_user`, `sys_account`, `sys_session`, `sys_organization`, `sys_member`, `sys_invitation`, `sys_file` and `sys_upload_session`, the `tenancy` service's `posture` / `isolationActive` / `degraded`, and `NODE_ENV`, `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE`, `OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY` and `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` after the boot.
  - At the file's first hook, the environment is identical, 168 variables each. The only difference was the probe's own output-path variable.
- **No mutation is owed.** The change moves where a first load is paid. It changes no tested behaviour, and no case asserts timing, so reverting it reddens nothing. The interleaved before leg is that revert, measured.

## Tests and gates (final head `56e42d33bf`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/organizations run typecheck`: exit 0. `check:test-typecheck` is OK, with 0 files in the debt ledger. `tsc --listFilesOnly` lists all 3 changed files in `tsconfig.test.json`, and the helper is also in `tsconfig.json`.
- The whole `@objectstack/organizations` suite with `--maxWorkers=2`: 13 of 13 files, 161 of 161 tests passed.
- ESLint on the 3 changed files with `--no-inline-config`: exit 0. The control-byte scan of the 3 files found 0 hits, and `check:nul-bytes` is OK.
- The helper sits under `src/__tests__/`, which `check:undeclared-dep-imports` reads as test code, so its imports of the devDependencies `@objectstack/verify` and `@objectstack/service-storage` are legal there.
- `skip-changeset`: the package ships `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. The helper's name has 0 hits in the built `dist`, and the positive control `OrganizationsPlugin` has 23.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 53 commands, the same 53 command lines as the seat's lead. All 53 exit 0 at `56e42d33bf`, each run separately with the exit code captured before any pipe, and `--ran` reports 53 derived, 53 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED and 0 UNRUN. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first answered exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, an unbuilt workspace) and exit 0 after a full `turbo run build` (75 of 75 tasks). No gate's output names any of the 3 changed files.
- `check:engine-double-contract` printed its repo-wide census line verbatim: `UNRECOGNISED [engine-double-contract]: 22 construct(s) in packages, examples declare a scanned verb (delete, update, findOne) alongside engine siblings, and this gate could not read the implementation -- so they are in NEITHER the pinned population nor the ledger.` This diff adds no construct.
- The full lint farm, Test Core, the dogfood jobs and the type-check lanes belong to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **The JSON span is not the graded number for hook-heavy files.** For a file whose wall sits in `beforeAll`, the JSON reporter's per-file `endTime - startTime` reads several times lower than the module line `report-test-timings.mjs` captures, because it spans the cases only. This is an observation for later slices' measurements, not a defect: the CI capture reads the module line, and that is the right number. No carrier is named.
- **One more file in this package boots through `bootStack`:** `walled-default-org-owner-bind-in-flight.pin.test.ts`. It is not on the card's list, and it is not measured here. Noted, not filed.
- The per-file CI captures cannot be read from this cloud container, as the previous slices also recorded. This is an environment fact, not a repo defect.
